title: The 7th Guest PAL and NTSC title-screen sizing
symptom: The NTSC title image appears taller and reaches both horizontal edges, while the PAL image appears less vertically stretched and retains narrow side columns.
expected: Each regional disc reproduces its real-hardware MPEG framing, VMPEG display window, and player pixel aspect; PAL and NTSC output need not be identical if their streams or guest programming differ.

input_events: allow the regional title MPEG to reach the 7th Guest logo frame

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The PAL and NTSC discs contain differently framed MPEG source pictures or intentionally program different VMPEG windows for their 625-line and 525-line players.
supporting_evidence: The supplied captures have different final raster sizes: NTSC is 720x539 and PAL is 768x574, both close to their expected 4:3 presentation sizes.
Regional MPEG encodes commonly use different coded heights and may retain different authored borders.
contradicting_evidence: The raw MPEG sequence dimensions, decoded-frame bounds, and live VMPEG window registers have not yet been compared.
A shared presentation defect could affect this title and the separately reported PAL/NTSC player-menu sizing.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Inventory both exact discs, compare MPEG sequence headers and a corresponding decoded frame before composition, then compare live VMPEG window and MCD212 external-video registers. Identical authored frames and guest register state with different normalized presentation would falsify this explanation.

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The NTSC DVC/MCD212/frontend path may use an incorrect vertical scale, horizontal aperture, or pixel-aspect conversion relative to PAL.
supporting_evidence: The NTSC logo and landscape appear taller, and the side columns visible in PAL are absent.
contradicting_evidence: The two captures are from different regional discs rather than the same authored frame under two player standards.
Both captured output sizes are already close to 4:3, so the difference may exist inside the authored MPEG picture or VMPEG window rather than at final window scaling.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Run one exact disc under both player standards and capture the decoded MPEG frame, external-video window, composed aperture, and frontend output. If only the regional disc changes the internal frame/window, host presentation is not the cause.

manual_verification.notes: User supplied NTSC 720x539 and PAL 768x574 screenshots and noted that either or both presentations may be correct.
